Every external package in the shipped closure (packages/coding-agent/npm-shrinkwrap.json) must appear here with a matching integrity hash and verdict "allow", or strape does not build (strape/scripts/reviewed-deps.mjs). Verdicts, tiers, capabilities and notes below were produced by an AGENT dependency review of the INSTALLED TARBALLS under node_modules (not upstream GitHub repos), recorded in strape/audit/dep-review-v0.84.0.md. An agent review is EVIDENCE, NOT SIGN-OFF: reviewedBy and reviewedAt are deliberately null on every entry and must be filled in by a human who has read the report and resolved each "escalate". Verdict "escalate" means a reviewer raised a concern, an adversarial second pass contradicted the first, or the artifact could not be read (native binaries, minified entry points) — those entries intentionally keep the gate failing until a human decides. Do not flip an escalate to allow without recording the reasoning in dep-review-v0.84.0.md. Tiers: A = high-consequence or capability-bearing (read in depth, 4 also got an adversarial second pass), B = small single-purpose utilities read in full, C = too large or not source-readable to review exhaustively (openai SDK, WASM, prebuilt native binaries) — the C boundary is stated plainly in the report.

@mariozechner/clipboard@0.3.9.notes: ESCALATE (Tier C: a stripped native ELF binary reads and writes the user's clipboard — this needs an explicit human accept). Zero lifecycle scripts on the main package AND all 10 optionalDependency sidecars (only dev-only napi build/test/prepublishOnly). index.js (25986 bytes) is plain readable auto-generated NAPI-RS loader code that deterministically selects ONE binary by platform/arch/musl detection and requires it by literal path — no untrusted string concatenation, no network. MIT, repository field (github.com/badlogic/clipboard, a fork of CrossCopy/clipboard over ChurchTao/clipboard-rs), and the documented API matches index.js's exports exactly. The live binary (clipboard.linux-x64-gnu.node, 1,378,264 bytes) is a stripped ELF64 shared object — opaque; `strings` shows only NAPI glue, Rust panic/std strings, X11/XFixes protocol names and Cargo provenance paths (napi-3.9.0, tokio-1.49.0, x11rb-0.13.2, image-0.25.5, rustix-1.1.3, base64-0.22.1, libloading-0.9.0), with NO hardcoded network host or URL of any kind. WHAT A HUMAN MUST DO: (1) accept that the machine code cannot be reviewed from node_modules — this verdict rests on integrity pinning, provenance strings matching the claimed Rust crate stack, zero install-time execution, and a narrow gated call site; for maximum assurance, reproducibly build clipboard-rs from the pinned upstream commit and diff. (2) independently re-verify the sha512 hashes here against the live npm registry — the review made NO outbound network call to do so. (3) note the loader honours NAPI_RS_NATIVE_LIBRARY_PATH from the environment (index.js:64-69) to override which .node gets required: generic NAPI-RS scaffolding, not remotely exploitable, but an attacker who already controls the developer's dotfiles can redirect clipboard loading to an arbitrary local binary. (4) weigh the value: strape calls only 4 of 17 exports (getText, setText, hasImage, getImageBinary) from packages/coding-agent/src/utils/clipboard-native.ts:14-23, gated on no TERMUX_VERSION and (non-Linux or DISPLAY/WAYLAND_DISPLAY set); watch(), RTF, HTML and clear() are unused surface on a package that by definition reads everything the user copies.

capabilities: none observable — no-op tracer/meter/propagator/diag interfaces plus a global symbol registry; no child_process, eval, fs writes, network, or process.env reads
